title: Brownsville Wellness Program for Blood Pressure
official: Brownsville Wellness Program for Blood Pressure (B-WELL BP): A Community-Based Food-is-Medicine Pilot
summary:
The Brownsville Wellness Program for Blood Pressure (B-WELL BP) is a community-based Food Is Medicine pilot study designed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a culturally tailored nutrition education program for adults with elevated blood pressure or hypertension in Brownsville, Brooklyn, New York.

The 6-week program will be delivered in partnership with the Brownsville Community Culinary Center (BCCC) and will incorporate nutrition education based on the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) eating pattern, cooking demonstrations, behavioral goal setting, weekly produce prescriptions, and a potassium-enriched salt substitute to support sodium reduction. The program will emphasize affordable, culturally relevant foods and practical strategies for improving dietary habits.

The study will enroll \~108 participants across three sequential cohorts, with a goal of approximately 90 participants completing the program. All participants will receive the intervention. There will be no randomized assignment or control group.

The primary dietary outcome will be change in diet quality, assessed using the rapid Prime Diet Quality Score (rPDQS). Secondary and exploratory outcomes will include changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, fruit and vegetable intake, body weight, and other health-related measures. The study will also evaluate recruitment, retention, attendance, participant engagement, intervention acceptability, implementation fidelity, and program costs.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 years or older.
* Reside in Brownsville, Brooklyn, New York, or receive services in the Brownsville community.
* Systolic blood pressure ≥120 and \<160 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure \<110 mmHg at screening.
* Able to attend weekly nutrition education sessions for the 6-week intervention.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unstable use of antihypertensive medications or glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists within the previous 6 months.
* Major illness or medical condition that would limit participation in the intervention.
* Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4 or 5).
* Pregnancy.
* Current participation in another nutrition intervention program.
